sections.html:
Dover is Delaware's capital and the seat of Kent County, and after Wilmington it is the state's second-largest city. State government is the biggest employer, Kent County government is another large one, and Dover Air Force Base in the southeast corner of the city anchors the rest of the local economy. Military orders arrive on a schedule that owners do not control, so some Dover sellers need to close fast once a move is ordered.

The city is flat and spread out along a handful of roads. US 13 is the Dupont Highway commercial strip, US 13 Alternate crosses downtown on Governors Avenue, DE 1 is a toll road east of town toward Wilmington and the beaches, DE 8 follows Division Street, and DE 15 serves the west side. Buyers who commute care about the distance to those roads more than about a neighborhood label.

William Penn founded Dover in 1683 as a court town, and the Green still holds the Kent County Courthouse and the Delaware Supreme Court. Twenty sites in the city are on the National Register of Historic Places, among them the Dover Green and Victorian Dover historic districts.

Owners of older houses downtown can run into design review for exterior work, and the city publishes guidelines for its historic districts. If your house is near the Green, call the planning office before you pay for a repair, so you learn whether it needs approval first.

Dover sits along the St. Jones River, and wind is a real concern here: a tornado tied to Tropical Storm Isaias in August 2020 caused damage in the city. A buyer or insurer will ask what you know about the roof and the drainage around the house, so put the answers on paper before you list.

  • Write down the age of the roof and any storm repairs.
  • Look up your parcel on the city's floodplain management page.
  • Gather receipts for HVAC replacement or service.
  • Photograph siding and any trees close to the house.

None of this changes what the house is worth, but a folder of records shortens the back and forth with an inspector.

A Dover owner pays tax twice, once to the city and once through Kent County, and the two follow separate calendars. The city rate is $0.485 per $100 of assessed value, applied to values set at 100 percent of January 1, 2020 fair market value. The city revalues every five years, most recently in 2020. City bills go out July 1, with supplemental bills in the first week of October, January and April.

Kent County's tax year runs June 1 to May 31. Its last reassessment took effect July 1, 2023. Bills usually reach owners by mid-August, and the full annual amount is due by September 30. Selling a house does not trigger a reassessment.

Reach the city tax office at 302-736-7005. The county assessment office is at 555 Bay Road, Dover, phone 302-744-2401.

Each April 1 the city puts its assessment register on display. Appeals are due April 30 by 5:00 p.m., and the city does not honor postmarks, so a letter sent on the final day arrives too late. Deliver it by hand or mail it well ahead.

Start by checking the record against the house itself: square footage, bathrooms, a finished basement, outbuildings. Factual errors are the simplest appeals to win. The county bill has its own January 31 window for annual assessments, and the county assessment office can walk you through it.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and recording a deed
sections.html:
Delaware charges a realty transfer tax that normally adds up to 4 percent: 2.5 percent to the state and 1.5 percent to the local government. By default buyer and seller each pay half, though a contract can shift that. First-time homebuyers can trim their half by 0.5 percent of up to $400,000, worth at most $2,000.

The Kent County Recorder of Deeds, at 555 Bay Road, records Dover deeds. Nothing goes on record until fees and taxes are paid, and a form with mistakes can cost a $40 nonconforming fee or a $20 rejection fee. Because an attorney must conduct the settlement in Delaware, that attorney ordinarily takes care of the filing.

An ordinance covering unincorporated areas sets a 1.5 percent transfer tax, but Dover is a city. Have your attorney confirm which local tax reaches a property inside the city.

A rental house in Dover needs an annual rental dwelling permit, which expires every January 31, and an owner who lives outside Kent County has to name a property manager based in the county. Settle the permit and any fees before the closing date.

Rentals of less than 30 days face limits. The 2021 ordinance says the owner must live in Dover and may only offer a primary residence, and the annual license is void once ownership transfers.

  • Under the vacant building article, a building counts as vacant after more than three consecutive months without occupants.
  • The owner registers within 30 days of the building going vacant and reports changes within 30 days.
  • Unpaid fees can land on the tax bill, and the city can insist on payment before title moves.

The planning office can confirm the latest wording and fees.

sections.h2: What Delaware requires you to disclose
sections.html:
Before a buyer can make an offer on a one to four unit home, Delaware wants a completed Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report, a written statement of every material defect you know about. Section 2577 carves out some transfers: estate, trust and guardianship transfers, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, sheriff's sales, and transfers among relatives.

Selling to us as-is means no repair list. You still complete the disclosure, and the attorney still runs the closing.

Most Dover sales, cash or financed, move through the same sequence:

  1. Choose a closing attorney first, because Delaware requires one to run the settlement.
  2. Collect the deed and your newest city and county tax bills.
  3. Phone the city tax office for a balance, and the planning office if the property is a rental or has stood vacant.
  4. Fill in the disclosure report truthfully and keep a copy for yourself.
  5. Get the closing date and the transfer tax split into the written agreement.

Paying cash removes the appraisal and loan approval, so closing can follow as soon as title work and the attorney's settlement are ready. A financed buyer needs both of those first.

faqs.q: How long does a house sale take in Dover, Delaware?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A cash sale can close as soon as the title work and the attorney settlement are ready, while a financed sale also needs appraisal and loan approval. Delaware requires an attorney to conduct the settlement either way.

faqs.q: When are Dover city property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Dover mails city tax bills on July 1, with supplemental bills in the first week of October, January and April. Kent County bills usually arrive by mid-August, and the annual tax is due by September 30.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for a Dover house?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Kent County Recorder of Deeds at 555 Bay Road in Dover. The office will not record a deed until the correct fees and taxes are collected.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems when selling my Dover house?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the sale is exempt. Delaware's Buyer Property Protection Act calls for a written disclosure of known material defects, with exemptions for court-ordered transfers, foreclosure sales and certain family transfers.

faqs.q: Does Dover Air Force Base affect selling a house here?
faqs.a: It can. Military orders move on a schedule, so some owners must sell on short notice, and a cash sale can fit that kind of deadline.
